runs.goal_hypothesis: Test whether an all-heuristic-heavy 10.24M-step curriculum with revised PPO settings learns broad competence across standard, defensive, and offensive heuristics.

results_insights.insight: Terminal aggregate performance was effectively zero.
At least one evaluated policy/side had no wins.
The only terminal wins were 2% as O against the generic heuristic; all defensive/offensive side rates were zero.

reasoning: The curriculum failed to convert heavy heuristic exposure into useful terminal competence.
The multi-knob regimen (opponent mixture, duration, entropy) prevents isolating one cause.
Evaluation sampling at 100 games per side adds uncertainty, but rates near zero make the failure unambiguous.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Retry the all-heuristic curriculum with a fixed 0.0001 learning rate and rebalanced heuristic mixture, relative to run 7de8435281814b42a4baa3beed4ce961.

results_insights.insight: The retry won none of its terminal evaluation games, versus 0.00333 aggregate in the predecessor.
Even the predecessor's small 2% generic-O success disappeared.

reasoning: The fixed learning rate and rebalanced mixture did not rescue the curriculum.
Because two configuration dimensions changed together, their individual effects are confounded.
Finite evaluation sampling cannot explain zero wins across every logged side/policy as evidence of broad competence.
